description: Resolves the one convention difference between this arc and qou-brng. Their L carries -(e/2) log(1-h) where my measured Markov traces give -log(z+d) alone. e is the WRITHE: the corpus's stacked_interface_writhe_normalised_probe tabulates mu_eff = mu (1-h)^(e/2) for sigma^m with e = m, and a bond sigma - beta h is the convex combination (1-beta) sigma + beta sigma^-1 (verified symbolically), so its expected writhe is 1 - 2 beta. pp (+1) and nn (-1) follow that; pn is passed 2 beta - 1 = -delta/2, the opposite convention, where the rule gives +delta/2. Correcting raises L_pn by 1.6133e-4 (0.0238%), worth 2.70e-3 MeV on 4He (0.0095%) — no conclusion moves, but L_pn is consumed by at least five probes so the fix belongs upstream. The deeper reconciliation: mine is the FRAMED trace ratio, theirs the WRITHE-NORMALISED one, which is why the -log(z+d) cores agreed to 1.3e-13 while the full L values did not. The choice is material — the writhe term raises p-p, lowers n-n and barely moves p-n, compressing the bond-type spread by 39%, which is what the mirror-pair ordering depends on — and which convention binding should use is a physics question (framing is Tw in Lk = Wr + Tw) not settled here. Per isotope the conventions differ by up to 6.4% of AME (3He) and ONLY where Z != N — at Z = N the p-p and n-n shifts are equal and opposite and cancel to under 0.02%, so the choice is invisible on 2H/4He/6Li and splits exactly the mirror pair. The no-distance-decay result survives both: the band generator's conjugator has net writhe zero, so far and adjacent bonds carry identical writhe.
caveats: WHICH CONVENTION BINDING SHOULD USE IS NOT SETTLED HERE. Framing is Tw in Lk = Wr + Tw, and the corpus carries a helicity thread where that decomposition is physical (Moffatt-Ricca, H = n Phi^2). If the nucleus is a framed object the framed trace is right; if the framing is gauge, the normalised one is. This probe only establishes that the two arcs are computing different objects and quantifies the gap — up to 6.4% of AME, all of it at Z != N — so that neither quotes across the line until someone decides.

THE pn SIGN IS REPORTED AS A DEFECT ON A SIBLING'S ACTIVE WORK, found by applying their own stated convention (e = writhe, from their own mu_eff tabulation) to their own three bonds. It is possible that pn's e is deliberately the other sign for a reason not written down — the source comment states the value but not a justification. Numerically it is 0.0095% on 4He, so nothing they have concluded depends on it either way.

The isotope table uses the NAIVE all-pairs sum for both conventions, so it isolates the framing choice. It therefore inherits the sub-additivity overstatement measured in pairwise_ceiling_is_overstated_probe and should not be read as a binding prediction in either column — only the DIFFERENCE between the columns is the quantity of interest here. Concretely: framed 3He lands at -0.01% of AME, which is a COINCIDENCE of the naive sum, not agreement. The measured H_9 trace of the same three-bond word gives 7.0196 against AME 7.71804.
